articles.title: Self-perceived masculinity and femininity predict political views better than biological sex
articles.summary: Moving beyond male and female demographic categories, new survey data reveals that how people internally perceive their own masculinity and femininity strongly predicts their political engagement, attitudes on gun rights, and broader ideological leanings.

articles.title: Alignment Faking Depends on the Value, Not Just the Model
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.03650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models can follow a directive when they believe they are monitored and abandon it when they believe they are not, a pattern termed Alignment Faking. Prior work establishes this for harmful-content objectives and a handful of moral-foundations values, leaving open how it distributes across a wider value space. We argue it is value-dependent: whether compliance survives a change in perceived oversight is a property of the model--value pairing, not of the model alone. articles.title: CARD: A Proof-Carrying Certificate-to-Action Interface for Relative-Measurement Graphs
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.03651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geometric certificates make mathematical claims about specified estimator objects, while robotic action requires a physical transform, a service decision, and timely proof support. We present CARD, a proof-carrying interface that keeps these objects distinct and records how they combine. Its lifted-fiber formulation separates semantic motion from witness repair and characterizes when projected and proof-carrying costs coincide. articles.title: Functional-Group Knowledge Is Structured in Language Models Before It Is Spoken
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.03684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models serve as the reasoning core of agents for chemistry and materials science, where they must interpret molecular structure before planning syntheses or proposing materials. Yet their outputs show only what they say, not what they know. Given a prompt such as ``The primary functional group in 1-Fluorobutane (CCCCF) is'', a small general-purpose model may answer ``the alkyne group'' instead of an alkyl fluoride. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.03654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cardiac auscultation traditionally detects the presence of a heart murmur, but clinicians further characterize it by timing, shape, pitch, quality, and grade. articles.title: Mixture of Wide Experts: Sparse Routing for Interpretable Native Coordinates
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.03655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models often spread a concept across many internal dimensions, making their features difficult to interpret. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) recover clearer features after training. We ask whether models can instead learn interpretable output coordinates directly. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.04041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Increasingly complex neural models predict blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) responses to naturalistic stimuli, but the predictive value of this added complexity remains unclear. articles.title: Curriculum unlearning in humans and neural networks
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.04565v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: During learning, humans often benefit from curricula that teach simple rules before exceptions. However, we lack a computational explanation for this phenomenon. Here, using a canonical behavioural task and modelling with neural networks, we develop and test a theory for why simple-to-complex curricula succeed. articles.title: Scientists discover new Alzheimer’s drug that repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that a drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries can tackle several key features of Alzheimer’s disease, including DNA damage and inflammation. Already tested for initial safety in humans, the experimental treatment could offer a faster path toward therapies that target the disease at its roots.

articles.title: Two kinds of political alienation pull support for violence in opposite directions, study finds
articles.summary: Feeling that your group is shut out of society is linked to support for political violence. But a survey in four European countries found that how people feel about politics can strengthen or weaken that link.

articles.title: New brain atlas reveals thousands of overlooked microproteins linked to Alzheimer’s disease
articles.summary: Researchers have mapped thousands of tiny, previously overlooked proteins in the human brain. This new atlas reveals that many of these hidden molecules are altered in Alzheimer's disease, offering new insights into brain aging and cellular energy production.

articles.title: The menstrual cycle may shape how much cannabis women use, new research suggests
articles.summary: Among people with premenstrual symptoms who used cannabis, the amount of dried flower they consumed tended to climb in the days before their period and again around ovulation, according to a study that tracked participants daily.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex?
